summary.en: You pay a large amount up front when you rent a room. A rough guide is 4 to 7 months of rent in total (it varies by region and property). Items: security deposit, key money, agent fee, damage insurance premium, rent (paid one month in advance in Japan), common service fee and others. The security deposit is held by the landlord and the remainder is returned after costs are settled when you move out (a rough guide is about 2 months of rent; to be checked). Key money is paid to the landlord and is not returned. In the Tokai region (which includes Aichi), Kansai and Kyushu, a "shikibiki" is common: a part of the deposit that is fixed in the lease as non-refundable. The agent fee is at most 1 month's rent plus tax in total, and at most half a month plus tax from you unless you agreed in advance. Key money, guarantee fees and renewal fees are separate (to be checked). Check whether an application fee is returned if no lease is made. Rent for a partial month is in principle prorated by day. If you use a guarantee company, a guarantee fee also applies. Ask for the amounts before you sign. Check the lease and ask the real estate agent (to be checked).
